short: The notes of a chord played one after another
definition: The notes of a chord played one after another instead of together.

short: Go straight on into the next movement, without a pause
definition: Italian for “attack”: the next movement begins at once, with no break, so the two are heard as one continuous piece.

short: A free solo passage while the orchestra waits
definition: A short solo passage where the rest of the orchestra stops and one player or singer is free to linger.

short: One melody chasing itself, like a round
definition: One instrument plays a melody and another follows a moment later with the same melody, like a round.

short: Smooth and expressive, in a singing style
definition: “In a singing style”: played smoothly and expressively, like a voice.

short: Slow, hymn-like music in solemn chords
definition: Slow, hymn-like music that moves in solemn chords.

short: The closing section that rounds off a movement
definition: A closing section added to the end of a movement.

short: Tapping the strings with the wood of the bow
definition: Tapping the strings with the wooden back of the bow, which makes a dry, clicking sound.

short: Getting gradually louder
definition: Getting gradually louder.

short: The middle of sonata form, where the themes are worked
definition: The middle stage of sonata form, where the themes are broken up, combined and pushed through different keys.

short: A medieval chant for the dead, a symbol of death
definition: A medieval chant from the Mass for the dead. Composers quote it as a symbol of death.

short: A string section split to play separate lines
definition: A string section split into two or more groups, each playing a different line.

short: The themes presented twice: orchestra, then soloist
definition: In the first movement of a Classical concerto, the main themes are presented twice: first by the orchestra alone, then by the soloist with the orchestra, this time moving to a new key.

short: Two notes played at once on a string instrument
definition: Bowing two strings at the same time, so that a single violinist or cellist sounds two notes together.

short: The opening of sonata form, where the themes are introduced
definition: The first stage of sonata form, where the main themes are introduced. It is often repeated.

short: A passage that begins like a fugue, then moves on
definition: A passage that starts like a fugue, with instruments entering one by one on the same tune, without being a full fugue.

short: One tune entering voice by voice, woven against itself
definition: A piece or section in which one tune enters in each voice in turn and is woven against itself.

short: A continuous slide from one note to another
definition: A continuous slide from one note to another.

short: Two bars of three beats regrouped into three pairs
definition: A rhythmic shift in which two bars of three beats are accented as if they were three groups of two, so they sound like one long bar of three slow beats. The beat seems to stumble or stretch.

short: Berlioz’s recurring melody that stands for a person
definition: “Fixed idea”: Berlioz’s term for a melody that represents a person and returns throughout a piece.

short: A rustic Austrian dance in three, ancestor of the waltz
definition: A rustic Austrian country dance in three beats, a slower, heavier ancestor of the waltz.

short: A German art song for voice and piano
definition: A German art song, usually a poem set for one voice with piano. Schubert wrote more than six hundred.

short: An old church scale: like a major scale with a raised fourth
definition: One of the old church modes. It sounds like a major scale with its fourth note raised a half step (F to F with B natural), which gives a bright, floating sound.

short: The kind of key that sounds bright or settled
definition: The kind of key that generally sounds bright or settled. Its darker counterpart is the minor.

short: An elegant 18th-century dance in three beats
definition: An elegant 18th-century dance in three beats, used as the third movement of Classical symphonies.

short: A short musical idea that keeps returning
definition: The smallest musical idea, just a few notes, from which a theme is built.

short: Played with a device that softens and veils the sound
definition: Played with a small device on the instrument that softens and veils the sound.

short: An essential, prominent solo instrumental part
definition: A solo instrumental part that is essential and prominent throughout a movement.

short: Players placed out of sight, heard from a distance
definition: Instruments placed behind the stage or outside the hall, so that they sound far away.

short: A short pattern repeated over and over
definition: A short rhythm or melody repeated persistently, often underneath changing music.

short: A short theme repeated while the music around it changes
definition: A form in which a short theme repeats over and over while the music around it keeps changing.

short: One note held in the bass under changing harmony
definition: A single note held or repeated, usually in the bass, while the harmony changes above it.

short: Plucking the strings instead of using the bow
definition: Plucking the strings of a string instrument with the finger instead of using the bow.

short: A small valveless horn once blown on mail coaches
definition: A small brass horn without valves, once blown by coachmen to announce the mail coach. It plays only a few notes, which gives it a simple, nostalgic sound.

short: Instrumental music that tells a story or paints a scene
definition: Instrumental music that tells a story or depicts a scene described by the composer.

short: The return of the opening themes near the end of sonata form
definition: The last stage of sonata form, where the opening themes return.

short: Music that follows the free rhythm of speech
definition: Music that imitates the rhythm of speech, free and unmeasured.

short: A main theme returning between contrasting episodes
definition: A form in which one main theme keeps returning between contrasting episodes.

short: A fast, energetic movement; the word means “joke”
definition: A fast, energetic movement, usually third in a symphony. The word means “joke”, though the mood is often far from funny.

short: A slow, swaying dance with a lilting long-short-long rhythm
definition: A slow, swaying piece in 6/8 or 12/8 with a lilting long-short-long rhythm, often used for gentle or melancholy music.

short: Three stages: exposition, development, recapitulation
definition: A three-stage structure: themes are introduced (exposition), worked and set against each other (development), and brought back (recapitulation).

short: The piano pedal that keeps notes ringing after release
definition: The piano’s right-hand pedal. It lifts the dampers off the strings, so notes keep ringing after the keys are let go and blend into one another.

short: Accents off the beat that pull against the pulse
definition: Accents placed off the main beats, which makes the rhythm feel as if it is floating or pulling against the pulse.

short: A whirling Italian dance in fast 6/8 time
definition: A fast, whirling folk dance from southern Italy in 6/8 time. Legend linked it to the bite of the tarantula spider.

short: A rapid shimmer between two notes, or on one
definition: A rapid back-and-forth between two notes, or the fast repetition of one, which makes a shimmering or rumbling sound. On the piano it is often an octave in the left hand.

short: A rapid shake between two neighbouring notes
definition: A rapid alternation between a note and the note just above it, which makes the sound shimmer or, low on the piano, rumble.

short: The gentler middle section of a minuet or scherzo
definition: The contrasting middle section of a minuet or scherzo, usually gentler.

short: The whole orchestra playing together
definition: Italian for “all”: the whole orchestra playing together, as opposed to the soloist.

short: Everyone playing the same notes at once
definition: Everyone playing the same notes at the same time.

short: A theme repeated with something changed
definition: A repeat of a theme in which something is changed: the decoration, the rhythm, the harmony or the instruments.

short: A horn-like brass instrument with a dark, soft tone
definition: A brass instrument made for Wagner’s Ring operas and played by horn players. Its tone is darker and rounder than a horn’s.
